_comment: Compute-unit classes with sourced capacities (data package B, item 6, 2026-10-23). Separate from partitions.json, which the model reads unchanged; these classes are for the schema-v3 model (hierarchy + block classes), not read by the current optimizer. Compute-unit classes with sourced capacities (2026-10-23, data package B, item 6). Not read by the model yet (config_reader reads only 'partition' and 'site'); they replace the provisional partition caps once the model reads schema v3. DMIPS: vendor figure where published, else cores x MHz x DMIPS/MHz of the core (Arm figures as listed in Wikipedia 'List of ARM processors': Cortex-M7 2.14, R52 2.09, A53 2.3, A76 10.7-12.4, A77 13-16; Cortex-A78 = A77 x 1.07 IPC, WikiChip / AnandTech 2020) and marked 'derived'. Prices: distributor single-unit prices (upper bound for OEM volume prices), USD; EUR/GBP converted at 1.10 / 1.30.

central_ad_gpu.example: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 64 GB module (proxy for DRIVE Orin)
central_ad_gpu.cpu_dmips_source: derived: 12 x 2200 MHz x 15.5 DMIPS/MHz (A77 13-16 x 1.07)
central_ad_gpu.gpu: 2048 CUDA + 64 Tensor cores (Ampere), 2x NVDLA v2, 1x PVA v2; 275 TOPS incl. DLA (GPU alone 170 sparse TOPS)
central_ad_gpu.asil_max: ASIL D systematic (NVIDIA DRIVE Orin SoC); the Jetson module itself is not AEC-Q100
central_ad_gpu.cost_source: NVIDIA launch price USD 1,599 per module at 1k units (GTC 2022, cnx-software.com 2022-03-22); 2026 retail GBP 2,111 (Scan UK)
central_ad_gpu.source: Connect Tech / NVIDIA module datasheet 900-13701-0050-000 (CPU, GPU, DLA, memory, eMMC, 1x GbE + 1x 10 GbE, 2x CAN, PCIe); clock 2.2 GHz: scan.co.uk listing

central_ad_soc.example: Renesas R-Car V4H (ADAS L2+/L3 central SoC; Toyota RAV4 2026 TSS unit by Denso)
central_ad_soc.cpu_dmips_source: Renesas product page 2026: 81 kDMIPS (2022 flyer: 49 kDMIPS; 4 x 1800 x 10.7-12.4 = 77-89k, so the page value is used)
central_ad_soc.rt_dmips_source: Renesas flyer 2022: 9 kDMIPS (page 2026 says 25k; 3 x 1400 x 2.09 = 8.8k, so the flyer value is used)
central_ad_soc.gpu: DL accelerator 34 TOPS (16 TOPS/W) + GPU AXM-8-256 at 600 MHz > 150 GFLOPS
central_ad_soc.ram: 64-bit LPDDR5-6400 interface; capacity is board-dependent (16 GB assumed, Whitebox-class board)
central_ad_soc.flash: external flash, board-dependent (64 GB assumed as the Orin class)
central_ad_soc.asil_max: ASIL B/D metrics (real-time domain ASIL D)
central_ad_soc.power_w: passive air cooling; no figure published
central_ad_soc.cost_source: not public (Renesas: "cost-competitive single-chip ADAS ECU"); use the Orin module price as the upper bound
central_ad_soc.source: Renesas R-Car V4H product page and flyer (renesas.com/products/r-car-v4h, 2022 flyer); ports: R-Car V4H Whitebox board (4 RGMII Ethernet, 8 CAN, 2 PCIe Gen4, 2 CSI2, 2 DSI)

zone_gateway.example: NXP S32G399A vehicle network processor (zonal gateway / zone controller)
zone_gateway.cpu_core: Cortex-A53 (2 clusters x 4; configurable as 4 lockstep pairs)
zone_gateway.cpu_dmips_source: derived: 8 x 1300 MHz x 3.0 DMIPS/MHz (NXP product brief: 2.8-3.2 DMIPS/MHz)
zone_gateway.ram: 20 MB SRAM with ECC on chip + DDR3L/LPDDR4 up to 4 GB

ports.note: 16 BCAN in the LLCE + 4 FlexCAN outside; LIN 4 + 3; FlexRay 1 dual-channel; 4 Ethernet MACs (3 PFE + 1 GMAC/TSN), two at 2.5 Gbps

zone_gateway.asil_max: ASIL D (lockstep clusters), two ASIL B independent clusters
zone_gateway.source: NXP S32G3 product brief PBS32G3V2 (cores, 1.3 GHz, 400 MHz M7, 20 MB SRAM, LPDDR4 up to 4 GB, LLCE 16 CAN / 4 LIN / 1 FlexRay, PFE, PCIe)

zone_realtime.example: NXP S32Z2 real-time processor (zonal / domain control, ASIL D)
zone_realtime.ram: 19 MB SRAM + LPDDR4 expansion interface (3.2 GB/s)

ports.note: 24 CAN FD via FlexLLCE; 2 Ethernet MACs + TSN Gigabit switch NETC3

zone_realtime.cost_source: not public; S32G399A price used as the proxy of the same NXP S32 class
zone_realtime.source: NXP S32Z2 product page (nxp.com/products/S32Z2) and S32E27 datasheet rev. 6, 2025

zone_mcu_classic.example: Infineon AURIX TC397 (classic zone / domain MCU; CARIAD measurement platform class TC39x)
zone_mcu_classic.cpu_dmips_source: Infineon datasheet summary: 4000 DMIPS (TriCore 1.7-2.4 DMIPS/MHz, Wikipedia: 510-720 per core)
zone_mcu_classic.cost_source: TC397XP256F300SBDKXUMA2 GBP 64.10 at 1 unit (Farnell UK, 2026-10-23; GBP 50.24 at 25+); budgetary EUR 50.29 per 1k (Mouser datasheet copy 2020)

ecu_small.example: NXP S32K344 (small body / sensor / actuator ECU)
ecu_small.cost_source: S32K344EHT1MPBST EUR 25.47 at 1 unit, EUR 18.68 at 100+ (Farnell IE, 2026-10-23)

reference_only.rh850_u2a16: Renesas RH850/U2A16 zone/domain MCU: 4 (+4 lockstep) G4MH cores at 400 MHz, 16 MB flash, 3.6 MB RAM, up to 16 CAN FD, 2x Ethernet AVB (Gbit/100 Mbit), ASIL D, 28 nm; DMIPS not published (renesas.com/products/rh850-u2a)
reference_only.measurement_host: Autoware was measured on AMD EPYC 7702 cores (Zen 2, 2.0 GHz base / 3.35 GHz boost, lightly loaded node) with an A100 GPU. Conversion to the central_ad_gpu class (A78AE 2.2 GHz): Betz et al. arXiv 2404.12683 measured the same Autoware chain 2.56x slower on Ampere Altra (Neoverse N1, 1.5 GHz; N1 = A76 class) than on EPYC 7313P (Zen 3, 3.0-3.7 GHz); A78 = 1.28x A76 per clock (Arm: A77 +20 %, A78 +7 %), 2.2/1.5 GHz clock ratio => an Orin core is 1.88x an Altra core => 1.36x slower than a 7313P core; a 7702 core (Zen 2, ~3.3 GHz boost) is ~0.75x a 7313P core (Zen 3 +19 % IPC, 3.7 GHz) => measured times on the host x 1.36 x 0.75 = x1.0 on an Orin core (derived, +-30 %; sensitivity case). V4H A76 core at 1.8 GHz: x1.6.
